title: Budget 2027 and your health: what changes for patients in Kuala Lumpur
desc: Budget 2027 gives the Health Ministry RM47.7 billion. What actually changes for patients in KL: medical bills, insurance, screening, waiting times, elderly care and tax relief.
headings: Budget 2027 health measures at a glance · Help with paying for treatment · MediAsas and private hospital bills · Shorter waits at government hospitals · Screening, fertility and vaccines · Elderly care · What it means for Kuala Lumpur · Tax relief changes for 2027 · What you can do now
keywords: Guides Budget 2027 and your health mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: The Health Ministry’s budget rises to RM47.7 billion in 2027, up from RM46.5 billion. MediAsas, an affordable basic medical insurance plan, launches in January 2027. EPF members under 55 can pay for it from Akaun Sejahtera. The Medical Assistance Fund for people who can’t afford treatment grows from RM40 million to RM60 million. PeKa B40 continues with RM80 million. Free thalassaemia screening is extended to the husbands and children of carriers. Two DBKL buildings in Taman Desa and Cheras will become senior daycare centres, and service tax on elderly care falls from 8% to 6%. The Madani Medical Scheme for minor illnesses at private GP clinics has no allocation in the 2027 estimates. Budget 2027 was tabled on 9 October 2026. These are the measures most likely to affect patients and families: Measure What it means for you MediAsas Basic medical insurance or takaful from January 2027, payable from EPF Akaun Sejahtera Medical Assistance Fund RM60 million (from RM40 million) for patients who can’t afford treatment PeKa B40 RM80 million for free screening and treatment support for STR recipients aged 40+ Thalassaemia screening Free for husbands and children of carriers Outsourcing to private hospitals RM200 million to send government patients to other facilities and shorten waits Private hospital bills Standard, transparent charge categories from 2027 Elderly care Service tax cut from 8% to 6%; two new senior daycare centres in KL Tax relief Medical relief extended to postnatal care; parents’ relief covers all care costs Most of these take effect in 2027. Tax changes still need to be passed in the Finance Bill. Medical Assistance Fund (Tabung Bantuan Perubatan): increased from RM40 million to RM60 million. It helps patients at government hospitals who can’t afford treatment or medical devices. Ask the hospital’s medical social work unit how to apply. PeKa B40: RM80 million, the same as in 2026. Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) recipients aged 40 and above, and their spouses, get free health screening, help with medical devices, and incentives to complete cancer treatment. Eligibility is automatic. MySalam: the free takaful protection scheme for lower-income Malaysians continues in 2027. Care aid for bedridden patients: the monthly aid for bedridden persons with disabilities and chronically ill patients rises from RM500 to RM600. The Madani Medical Scheme The Madani Medical Scheme (Skim Perubatan Madani) subsidised visits to private GP clinics for minor illnesses such as fever, diarrhoea and headaches for lower-income Malaysians. Its funding was halved to RM50 million in 2026, and CodeBlue reports it has no allocation in the Health Ministry’s 2027 estimates. The government has not announced an end date. If you rely on it, ask your clinic whether it is still accepting the scheme. Government health clinics (Klinik Kesihatan) remain a low-cost option for minor illnesses. MediAsas is a basic medical insurance and takaful plan that launches in January 2027 . It is designed to be affordable for people who have no medical cover or have dropped a plan they could no longer pay for. Under Budget 2027: EPF members under 55 can pay MediAsas premiums from their Akaun Sejahtera . Companies with fewer than 75 staff get a RM200 subsidy for each employee’s first-year premium, for up to 50 employees. About 200,000 workers are expected to benefit. Hospitals will be paid by diagnosis and type of treatment (Diagnosis Related Groups), which aims to make costs more predictable. Separately, from 2027 private hospitals must use standard, transparent charge categories on their bills, so patients can see and compare what they are paying for. See our full guide: MediAsas explained: cover, premiums and who it suits . Outsourcing to other facilities: the allocation for sending government patients elsewhere rises to RM200 million. It now includes using private facilities, including operating theatres, and covers expanded newborn screening, prenatal genetic tests and rehabilitation. More specialists: retired government specialists and private specialists can work sessions at government hospitals on more flexible terms and for longer. More permanent doctors: more than 9,000 contract doctors will be offered permanent posts in 2027. The monthly incentive for about 47,000 nurses and paramedics with post-basic training doubles from RM100 to RM200. Ambulances and equipment: more than RM770 million for medical equipment, including 400 new ambulances and upgraded haemodialysis facilities. The new ambulances matter. In 2025, only about a third of the most urgent emergency calls were reached within the 15-minute target. In an emergency, always call 999 . If you are unsure whether you need an ambulance, see our guide to clinic or emergency department . Thalassaemia: free screening at Ministry of Health facilities is extended to the husbands and children of carriers . Thalassaemia is an inherited blood disorder. Two carriers have a 1 in 4 chance in each pregnancy of having a child with thalassaemia major, who needs lifelong blood transfusions. Screening helps couples know their risk. Fertility (BuAi programme): subsidised fertility treatment (intrauterine insemination) for 2,000 couples through LPPKN, and men’s wellness services for 42,000 people. HPV vaccine: the school programme for about 230,000 Year 6 girls moves to a vaccine that covers nine HPV types instead of two. See our HPV vaccine guide . Drivers: commercial vehicle drivers get PERKESO health screening vouchers worth up to RM30. Mobile clinics: 10 university teaching hospitals will run screening and mobile clinics for lower-income, vulnerable and rural communities. For free screening you can already use, see free health screening in Malaysia 2026 . Service tax on elderly care falls from 8% to 6% from 1 January 2027, and care fees of up to RM96,000 a year are fully exempt from service tax. Two senior daycare centres in Kuala Lumpur: two DBKL buildings, at the Anjung Kelana homeless transformation centre in Taman Desa and the Cheras temporary market, will be upgraded into senior daycare centres. Opening dates have not been announced. Getting around KL: 22 km of covered walkways, including links from homes to clinics, and buggies for older visitors at Tugu Negara, the Perdana Botanical Gardens and Carcosa. Bantuan Warga Emas: RM1.3 billion for about 200,000 recipients. A Senior Citizens Bill is also planned. Budget 2027 extends tax relief to all care costs for parents and grandparents, not only medical bills. None of the four new health facilities named in the budget speech are in Kuala Lumpur. They are in Johor, Kuching, Gerik and Rembau. For KL residents, the most visible changes are likely to be: Hospital Kuala Lumpur (HKL) is one of 16 hospitals rolling out a full Hospital Information System in 2027, with RM200 million for the initiative. HKL’s director said the aim is a fully computerised hospital, so patients don’t have to repeat their medical history at every stage of care. Lift replacement is under way, and electrical and IT upgrades are planned. Linked medical records: a separate RM1 billion investment by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will connect electronic records across 150 hospitals and 2,488 health clinics under a “one person, one record” approach, with telehealth services. Repairs and air-conditioning: RM1.2 billion for maintaining public hospitals and clinics nationwide, including new air-conditioning at 600 Ministry of Health clinic facilities. The two senior daycare centres in Taman Desa and Cheras, and new covered walkways. These apply from the 2027 year of assessment, once passed in the Finance Bill: Medical expenses relief is extended to postnatal care . News reports say the overall limit stays at RM10,000, with postnatal care capped at RM3,000 within it. Vaccinations, health screening, dental treatment and fertility treatment remain claimable. Relief for parents and grandparents now covers all care expenses, not only medical treatment. Individual relief rises from RM9,000 to RM12,000. Keep receipts for medical, screening, vaccination and care expenses. Check the final rules with LHDN before filing. If you are 40 or over, check whether you qualify for free screening through PeKa B40 or PERKESO, and book it before the year ends. If you have no medical insurance, or are struggling with premiums, compare your current plan with MediAsas when insurers publish prices. Don’t cancel an existing policy until new cover is in place. If thalassaemia runs in your family, ask your Klinik Kesihatan about free screening for your spouse and children. If you care for an older parent, keep receipts for care costs, which can be claimed under the expanded relief from 2027. How much does the Health Ministry get in Budget 2027? RM47.7 billion, up from about RM46.5 billion in 2026, an increase of RM1.18 billion. When does MediAsas start? January 2027. EPF members under 55 can pay MediAsas premiums from their Akaun Sejahtera, and small companies get a RM200 subsidy per employee for the first year. Who can get free thalassaemia screening under Budget 2027? Free screening at Ministry of Health facilities is extended to the husbands and children of thalassaemia carriers. Ask at your nearest Klinik Kesihatan. Is the Madani Medical Scheme continuing in 2027? CodeBlue reports that the scheme has no allocation in the Health Ministry’s 2027 estimates, after its funding was halved in 2026. No end date has been announced, so check with your clinic. Are there new senior daycare centres in Kuala Lumpur? Yes. Two DBKL buildings, in Taman Desa and at the Cheras temporary market, will be upgraded into senior daycare centres. Opening dates have not been announced. What medical tax relief changes in 2027? Medical expenses relief is extended to postnatal care, and parents’ relief covers all care expenses, not only medical bills. These still need to be passed in the Finance Bill.

title: MediAsas explained: Malaysia’s basic medical insurance plan from January 2027
desc: MediAsas is a basic medical insurance and takaful plan launching in January 2027. Teras and Fleksi compared, what it covers, the main exclusions, expected premiums and who it suits.
headings: Why MediAsas was created · Teras and Fleksi: the two plans · What MediAsas covers · What it doesn’t cover · Who can buy it · How much will it cost? · How hospitals are paid, and why it matters · Should you get MediAsas?
keywords: Guides MediAsas explained denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: MediAsas is a standardised basic medical insurance and takaful plan backed by Bank Negara Malaysia and the Ministry of Finance. It launches nationwide in January 2027. There are two versions: Teras, with an annual limit of RM100,000 (RM150,000 from age 60) and a small deductible, and Fleksi, with a RM300,000 limit and a RM10,000 deductible, meant to top up employer cover. It is voluntary and fully underwritten. Pre-existing conditions are not covered, and there are 35 main exclusions. Final premiums have not been published. The government has indicated about RM60 to RM550 a month, depending on age. EPF members under 55 can pay premiums from Akaun Sejahtera. Don’t cancel an existing plan until new cover is in place. Medical costs in Malaysia rose about 15% in 2024, and many insurers raised premiums sharply. Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) stepped in with interim measures in December 2024, asking insurers to spread increases over at least three years. Even so, about 340,000 medical policies were surrendered between January 2024 and June 2025, according to BNM’s white paper on medical insurance. MediAsas, first called the “Base MHIT plan”, is the result. It is a simple, standard plan, the same at every provider, with cost-sharing and hospital payment rules designed to keep premiums affordable over the long term. MediAsas comes in two versions, each offered as conventional insurance or as takaful. These figures are from BNM’s pilot programme. BNM says benefits may change in the final version launched in January 2027. MediAsas Teras MediAsas Fleksi Who it is for People with no other medical cover People with employer or other cover who want protection for large bills Annual limit RM100,000 (RM150,000 from age 60) RM300,000 Lifetime limit None None Deductible RM500 per illness or injury (RM1,000 from age 60) at network hospitals RM10,000 a year at network hospitals, RM15,000 elsewhere Outside the hospital network Deductible plus 20% co-payment, capped at RM3,000 Higher deductible No deductible for Government hospitals, emergencies and outpatient cancer treatment No waivers A deductible is the amount you pay yourself before the plan pays. A co-payment is a share of the bill you pay on top. Both help keep premiums lower. Hospital stays: a shared room (two or four beds), intensive care, surgery and day surgery, and ambulance. You can upgrade to a single room, but you pay the difference. Before and after hospital: tests and consultations up to 30 days before admission and 90 days after, including physiotherapy, home nursing and the GP visit that referred you. Cancer: outpatient cancer treatment such as chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Some outpatient care at hospitals: dengue, influenza, bronchitis and pneumonia, up to RM3,000 a year. It does not cover treatment overseas, and there is no no-claim bonus. MediAsas also pays for the GP visit that refers you to hospital, and for follow-up after discharge. BNM lists 35 main exclusions. The most important are: Pre-existing conditions , and congenital or hereditary conditions Mental and nervous disorders Pregnancy, childbirth and fertility treatment Dental treatment, spectacles and eye surgery to correct vision Cosmetic surgery and weight management Implanted devices such as pacemakers and hearing aids Sexually transmitted infections, including HIV Self-harm, substance misuse and hazardous sports There is also a 30-day waiting period for illness (accidents are covered straight away) and a 120-day waiting period for specified illnesses. Read the full list of exclusions in the policy before you buy. Age: you can join from birth up to age 70, and renew each year up to age 85. Residency: the pilot was limited to Malaysian citizens. BNM says permanent residents and foreigners living in Malaysia will be able to join at the national launch. Health questions: MediAsas is fully underwritten. You must answer a health questionnaire honestly, and the insurer can decline you, charge more, or exclude a condition. BNM has said some well-managed conditions may be accepted. One plan only: you can hold only one MediAsas policy at a time. If you cancel it, you must go through underwriting again to rejoin. If you didn’t disclose something by mistake, the insurer can’t dispute a claim on that basis after seven years, except for fraud, deliberate non-disclosure, or major illnesses such as cancer, organ failure and serious heart disease that existed before cover started. Final premiums have not been published. The government has indicated a range of about RM60 to RM550 a month , depending on your age when you join, with the lowest premiums for younger people. Insurers will publish prices closer to the January 2027 launch. Premiums are not guaranteed. They rise as you get older, and can be reviewed for everyone in the plan based on how the whole MediAsas pool performs, with at least 30 days’ written notice. Your premium does not go up just because you made a claim. BNM plans an independent governance board to review prices each year. Ways to pay under Budget 2027: EPF members under 55 can pay premiums from Akaun Sejahtera (Account 2). Companies with fewer than 75 staff get RM200 off each employee’s first-year premium , for up to 50 employees. How employers claim this has not yet been announced. Premiums may also qualify for income tax relief on medical insurance, subject to LHDN’s rules. MediAsas network hospitals are paid a set amount for each type of diagnosis and treatment, known as Diagnosis Related Groups (DRG) , instead of item by item. This aims to stop costs rising unpredictably, which keeps premiums stable. For you, the deductible and limits stay the same. BNM’s example: a hospital stay for food poisoning billed at RM12,000 might be paid at RM10,000 under DRG. Separately, Budget 2027 requires all private hospitals to use standard, transparent charge categories on bills from 2027. You have no medical cover: Teras is designed for you. Compare prices when they are published in early 2027. You only have employer cover: employer plans usually end when you leave the job and may have low limits. Fleksi is designed to sit on top for large bills. You already have a personal plan: BNM says MediAsas is meant to complement existing cover, not replace it. Compare limits, room and board, exclusions and premiums carefully. Your current plan may cover conditions MediAsas excludes, especially if you have developed a condition since you bought it. You are on a low income: PeKa B40 and MySalam already give free protection to eligible Malaysians. Government hospitals remain heavily subsidised. Don’t cancel your current plan first If you cancel an existing policy, any condition you have developed since it started is likely to count as pre-existing under MediAsas and won’t be covered. Only change plans once new cover has been approved and you have compared what you would lose. When does MediAsas start? MediAsas launches nationwide in January 2027. A pilot with six insurers and takaful operators and 10 private hospitals ran in the Klang Valley from July 2026. How much is MediAsas a month? Final premiums have not been published. The government has indicated about RM60 to RM550 a month, depending on your age when you join. What is the difference between MediAsas Teras and Fleksi? Teras is a basic plan with an annual limit of RM100,000 (RM150,000 from age 60) and a deductible of RM500 per illness at network hospitals. Fleksi has a RM300,000 limit and a RM10,000 yearly deductible, and is meant to top up employer cover. Does MediAsas cover pre-existing conditions? No. MediAsas is fully underwritten and excludes pre-existing conditions. Some well-managed conditions may be accepted at the insurer’s discretion. Can I use EPF to pay for MediAsas? Yes, if you are under 55. Budget 2027 allows EPF members to pay MediAsas premiums from Akaun Sejahtera. Should I cancel my current medical insurance for MediAsas? Not without comparing carefully and getting new cover approved first. Conditions you developed after buying your current plan would likely be excluded as pre-existing under MediAsas.

title: World Diabetes Day 2026: how and where to get your blood sugar checked in KL
desc: World Diabetes Day falls on Saturday 14 November. Which test to ask for, what the numbers mean under Malaysian guidelines, free ways to get tested in KL, and what to do if you have prediabetes.
headings: This year’s theme: early action · Who should get tested · Which test to ask for · What your results mean · If you have prediabetes · Free and low-cost tests in Kuala Lumpur · When high blood sugar is an emergency
keywords: Heart & diabetes World Diabetes Day 2026 Diabetes mellitus Kencing manis kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: World Diabetes Day is on Saturday 14 November 2026. The theme for 2026–27 is “Early action on diabetes”. 15.6% of Malaysian adults have diabetes, and two in five of them don’t know it. Malaysia diagnoses diabetes at an HbA1c of 6.3% or above, lower than the 6.5% used in many other countries. 5.7% to 6.2% is prediabetes. A finger-prick reading is only a first screen. Diabetes is confirmed with a blood test from a vein, usually repeated. Free tests are available at Klinik Kesihatan (book in MySejahtera), through PeKa B40 and PERKESO, and at Diabetes Malaysia’s KL event on 14 November. The International Diabetes Federation has chosen “Early action on diabetes” as the World Diabetes Day theme for 2026 and 2027. It focuses on finding diabetes sooner and lowering the risk for people who don’t have it yet. Globally, about 1 in 9 adults has diabetes, and up to half already have complications by the time they are diagnosed. In Malaysia, the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2023 found diabetes in 15.6% of adults , about 3.6 million people. Two in five didn’t know they had it, and more than half of those who did know didn’t have their blood sugar under control. On 6 October 2026, the Health Minister told Parliament that more than 80% of adults aged 18 to 29 with diabetes are undiagnosed. We covered those figures in undiagnosed diabetes and high blood pressure in young Malaysians . Malaysia’s Clinical Practice Guidelines recommend a blood sugar test for everyone from age 30 , repeated every year if normal. Get tested earlier , at any adult age, if you: have a BMI over 23 (lower than the international overweight cut-off of 25, because Asians tend to develop diabetes at lower weights) have a parent, brother or sister with diabetes had diabetes in pregnancy have polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), heart disease, or abnormal cholesterol are mostly inactive, or take medicines such as long-term steroids If you have prediabetes, you should be tested every year. A finger-prick glucose test is a useful first check, but it can’t diagnose diabetes on its own. Test How it works Fasting? HbA1c Shows your average blood sugar over the last 2–3 months No Fasting plasma glucose Blood sugar after an overnight fast Yes, at least 8 hours Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) Blood sugar before and 2 hours after a 75 g glucose drink Yes; plain water only, rest during the test Finger-prick (capillary) glucose A quick screen with a glucometer Either HbA1c is the most convenient, because you don’t need to fast. It is less reliable if you are anaemic, have kidney disease, take iron supplements or steroids, or have a haemoglobin variant such as thalassaemia trait. Your doctor may use a glucose test instead. A finger-prick test at a pharmacy, event or at home is only a first screen. If it reads 5.6 mmol/L or higher fasting, or 7.8 mmol/L or higher at any time, see a doctor for a proper blood test. These are the cut-offs in Malaysia’s Clinical Practice Guidelines (2020), for blood taken from a vein: Test Normal Prediabetes Diabetes HbA1c Below 5.7% 5.7% to 6.2% 6.3% or above Fasting glucose Below 6.1 mmol/L 6.1 to 6.9 mmol/L 7.0 mmol/L or above 2 hours after glucose drink (OGTT) Below 7.8 mmol/L 7.8 to 11.0 mmol/L 11.1 mmol/L or above Random glucose — — 11.1 mmol/L or above, with symptoms Malaysia uses an HbA1c of 6.3% to diagnose diabetes, lower than the 6.5% used in many countries. Local research found 6.5% would miss too many Malaysians with diabetes. If you have no symptoms , diabetes is diagnosed only after two abnormal results , either two different tests on the same blood sample or the same test on two occasions. One abnormal result is enough if you also have symptoms such as thirst, passing a lot of urine, or weight loss. Prediabetes means your blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet in the diabetes range. This is where early action works best. In a large US trial, a lifestyle programme cut the number of people with prediabetes who went on to develop type 2 diabetes by 58% , and by 71% in people over 60. Malaysian guidelines recommend: Losing at least 7% of your body weight if you are overweight. For a 75 kg person, that is about 5 kg. At least 150 minutes of activity a week , such as brisk walking for 30 minutes on five days. Cutting sweet drinks and refined carbohydrates. Fill half your plate with vegetables, a quarter with protein and a quarter with whole grains, following the Suku-Suku Separuh guide. A blood sugar test every year. Your doctor may also suggest medicine if your risk is high. Thirty minutes of brisk walking on five days a week meets the activity target for preventing diabetes. Klinik Kesihatan: government health clinics offer free blood sugar, blood pressure, BMI and cholesterol checks under the National Health Screening Initiative. Book in the MySejahtera app under Appointments, then NHSI. Your results appear in the app. More than 2.65 million people have been screened since 2022. PeKa B40: free screening, including blood sugar, for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah recipients aged 40 and above, and their spouses. Check your eligibility with your IC number on the PeKa B40 website. PERKESO Health Screening Programme: a free, one-time screening for PERKESO contributors aged 40 to 59, booked through the SEHATi app. Diabetes Malaysia’s KL event: Diabetes Malaysia lists a World Diabetes Day state event in Kuala Lumpur on Saturday 14 November, 9am to 4pm . The venue had not been announced at the time of writing. Call Diabetes Malaysia on 03-7957 4062 for details. For more on these programmes, see free health screening in Malaysia 2026 . Any GP clinic can also do an HbA1c or fasting glucose test. Very high blood sugar can cause diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or a hyperosmolar state (HHS). Both are medical emergencies, and they are sometimes the first sign of undiagnosed diabetes, especially in older people. Go to an emergency department or call 999 if someone has Vomiting or stomach pain with high blood sugar Fast or deep breathing, or a fast heartbeat Fruity-smelling breath Drowsiness or confusion Extreme thirst and passing a lot of urine, with weakness Don’t drive yourself. See our guide to clinic or emergency department . When is World Diabetes Day 2026? Saturday 14 November 2026. The theme for 2026 and 2027 is “Early action on diabetes”. What HbA1c level means diabetes in Malaysia? An HbA1c of 6.3% or above, confirmed by a second abnormal result if you have no symptoms. An HbA1c of 5.7% to 6.2% is prediabetes. Do I need to fast for a diabetes test? Not for an HbA1c test. For a fasting glucose test or an oral glucose tolerance test, fast for at least 8 hours beforehand. Plain water is fine. Can a glucometer diagnose diabetes? No. A finger-prick reading is a first screen only. If it is high, a doctor will confirm with a blood test from a vein, such as fasting glucose, HbA1c or an OGTT. Where can I get a free diabetes test in KL? At government health clinics (book through MySejahtera under NHSI), through PeKa B40 if you are an STR recipient aged 40+, or through PERKESO’s screening programme if you are a contributor aged 40–59. Can prediabetes be reversed? Often, yes. Losing at least 7% of body weight and doing 150 minutes of activity a week can bring blood sugar back to normal and greatly lowers the risk of type 2 diabetes.

title: Free health screening in Malaysia 2026: PERKESO, PeKa B40, Selangor Saring and more
desc: Several free health screening programmes run in Malaysia in 2026. Who qualifies for each, what they test, how to book, and which checks you need at your age.
headings: Why get screened if you feel fine? · Free screening programmes at a glance · PERKESO Health Screening Programme (HSP 2026) · PeKa B40 (for STR recipients aged 40+) · Free checks at government health clinics · Selangor Saring 2026 · What Budget 2027 changes · Which screenings you need at your age · How to prepare, and what to do with your results
keywords: Prevention Free health screening in Malaysia kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october kesihatan mental depression anxiety stress kemurungan mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: PERKESO’s Health Screening Programme (HSP 2026) is free, once only, for Malaysian workers aged 40–59 who meet the contribution rules. Check and book in the SEHATi app. PeKa B40 is free for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) recipients aged 40 and above, and their spouses. No registration is needed. Government health clinics (Klinik Kesihatan) offer free basic checks for blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol, BMI and mental health. Selangor Saring runs free community screening days across the state until December. Register in the SELangkah app. Budget 2027 keeps PeKa B40 going and adds PERKESO screening vouchers for commercial vehicle drivers. High blood pressure, diabetes and high cholesterol usually cause no symptoms for years. By the time they do, they may already have damaged the heart, kidneys or eyes. Screening finds them early, when they are easier to treat. Recent Malaysian figures show how common hidden problems are. Among PERKESO contributors screened between 2023 and 2025, mostly aged 40–59, 59.2% were overweight or obese , about 19% had diabetes and 17.45% had high blood pressure. In PeKa B40’s 2025 screening, 44.37% of participants had diabetes, high blood pressure or high cholesterol. Blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol checks are part of every free screening programme below. Programme Who it is for How to book PERKESO HSP 2026 Malaysian workers aged 40–59 who meet PERKESO’s contribution rules, once only SEHATi app, then a panel clinic PeKa B40 STR recipients aged 40+, and their spouses Automatic; go to a PeKa B40 clinic with your MyKad Klinik Kesihatan (NHSI) Everyone; free basic checks Walk in, or book through MySejahtera Selangor Saring Selangor residents SELangkah app; sessions until December Rules can change during the year, so check the official app or website for each programme before you go. PERKESO (SOCSO) offers a free health screening to working Malaysians. The current edition, listed as HSP 2026 in PERKESO’s SEHATi help pages, continues the HSP 3.0 programme that began in 2023. Who qualifies: Malaysian citizens aged 40 to 59 At least one month of Invalidity Scheme (Skim Keilatan) contributions in the current year, and at least 12 months of contributions in total You have not had an HSP screening before . It is a one-time benefit, not a yearly one. What is tested in 2026: a physical examination and family history, full blood count, HbA1c (average blood sugar), a fasting cholesterol profile, a urine test and a mental health screening, followed by a review of your results with a doctor. Women are also offered a Pap smear and a mammogram. For a small extra charge you can add blood group, liver and kidney tests. How to book: download the SEHATi app, check your eligibility and choose a panel clinic. The clinic will confirm your eligibility with your IC number. If you are not eligible, SEHATi also lists paid screening packages for PERKESO contributors. PERKESO has not published a closing date for 2026, so check the SEHATi app for the latest details. PeKa B40 is a government scheme run by ProtectHealth for lower-income Malaysians. You qualify if you are a Malaysian aged 40 or above and receive Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) , or are the spouse of a recipient. Eligibility is automatic, so there is nothing to register. The free screening covers your health history and risk factors, a physical examination, blood and urine tests, a mental health screening, and a breast examination for women or a prostate examination for men at risk. It is done at private GP clinics registered with PeKa B40. You can check your eligibility with your IC number on the PeKa B40 website. Since 2019 the scheme has served more than 1.9 million people. Budget 2027 allocates RM80 million to continue it. Under the National Health Screening Initiative (NHSI), government health clinics and PeKa B40 clinics offer free basic screening for blood sugar, blood pressure, BMI, cholesterol and mental health . If a result is abnormal, you are referred for confirmatory tests and follow-up. You can walk in to your nearest Klinik Kesihatan or book an appointment through the MySejahtera app. Government clinics also run other free or low-cost screenings, such as cervical screening and mammogram referrals for women. See our guide to breast cancer screening and free mammograms . Selangor Saring is the Selangor state government’s free health screening programme, run with Selcare since 2022. In 2026 it has RM2.5 million in funding and runs from January to December , mostly at weekends, across the state’s 56 constituencies. Depending on your risk, tests at the screening days can include heart, blood pressure, diabetes and kidney checks, screening for breast, cervical, colorectal and prostate cancer, and eye, dental and hearing checks. How to register: fill in the screening form in the SELangkah app, then choose a location and date. Some sessions accept walk-ins, but booking first is safer. The Selcare helpline is 1-800-22-6600. Budget 2027, tabled on 9 October 2026, includes several screening measures: PeKa B40 continues , with RM80 million for free screening and treatment support for STR recipients and their spouses aged 40+. Screening vouchers for commercial vehicle drivers , worth up to RM30, through PERKESO. Free thalassaemia screening at MOH facilities extended to the husbands and children of families who carry the gene. Screening and mobile clinics run by university teaching hospitals for rural and lower-income communities. Malaysia’s Ministry of Health Clinical Practice Guidelines recommend these checks for adults at average risk. Your doctor may advise earlier or more frequent tests if you have risk factors or a family history. Check Who and how often Blood pressure All adults over 18, at least once a year Blood sugar (diabetes) From age 30, yearly if normal. Earlier if you are overweight and have another risk factor, or had diabetes in pregnancy Cholesterol All adults over 30. From 18 if you are at high risk, for example with a strong family history Cervical screening Women aged 30–49: HPV test, every 5 years if negative. Pap smear at ages 21–29 and 50–65 Breast (mammogram) Every 2 years for women aged 50–74. Earlier for women at high risk Bowel (colorectal) Ages 50–75: a stool test (iFOBT) every year, with colonoscopy if positive Ask whether you need to fast. If your tests include a fasting blood test, you will usually be asked not to eat for 8 to 10 hours beforehand. Plain water is fine. Bring your MyKad, a list of any medicines you take, and any previous results. Don’t skip the results review. A screening only helps if abnormal results are followed up. If a result is borderline or high, ask what the next step is and when to repeat the test. Screening is not for symptoms If you already have symptoms, such as chest pain, unexplained weight loss, a breast lump or blood in your stool, see a doctor now rather than waiting for a screening day. For chest pain or difficulty breathing, call 999. Who is eligible for the free PERKESO health screening in 2026? Malaysian citizens aged 40 to 59 with at least one month of Invalidity Scheme contributions this year, at least 12 months in total, and no previous HSP screening. Check your eligibility in the SEHATi app. Can I do the PERKESO health screening every year? No. The HSP is a one-time benefit. If you have already had an HSP screening, PERKESO contributors can book paid packages through the SEHATi app instead. How do I know if I qualify for PeKa B40? If you are a Malaysian aged 40 or above and receive Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), or are the spouse of a recipient, you qualify automatically. You can check with your IC number on the PeKa B40 website. Is health screening free at Klinik Kesihatan? Yes, basic screening for blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol, BMI and mental health is free at government health clinics under the National Health Screening Initiative. You can book through MySejahtera. How do I register for Selangor Saring? Fill in the screening form in the SELangkah app and choose a location and date. Sessions run across Selangor until December 2026, mostly at weekends.

title: Dengue vaccine in Malaysia: what Qdenga can and can’t do
desc: With dengue cases up sharply in 2026, many people are asking about the vaccine. Who can get it, how well it works, the important DENV-3 caveat, and what it costs.
headings: Dengue in Malaysia in 2026 · What is the dengue vaccine? · Who can have it, and who should not · How well does it work? · The DENV-3 caveat · Side effects · Cost and where to get it · Keep preventing bites, even if vaccinated
keywords: Prevention Dengue vaccine in Malaysia Dengue Denggi denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Qdenga is the only dengue vaccine available in Malaysia. It is conditionally registered for people aged 4 and above, given as two doses three months apart. It is not part of the National Immunisation Programme, so it is only available at private clinics and hospitals. In trials it cut dengue hospitalisations by about 84% over four and a half years. In people who have never had dengue, it did not protect against DENV-3, the strain driving Malaysia’s 2026 surge. Discuss this with your doctor. The vaccine does not replace mosquito control or knowing the warning signs of severe dengue. Malaysia recorded 78,225 dengue cases and 68 deaths between 4 January and 25 October 2026, according to the national iDengue portal. Selangor accounts for the largest share, followed by the Federal Territories and Johor. By early September, cases were 66% higher than in the same period of 2025, and deaths had almost doubled. The Ministry of Health has linked the rise to a shift in the dominant dengue strain, from DENV-2 to DENV-3 . That matters when thinking about the vaccine, as explained below. Dengue is spread by Aedes mosquitoes, which bite mostly in the early morning and late afternoon. Qdenga (also known as TAK-003) is a live, weakened vaccine designed to protect against all four types of dengue virus (DENV-1 to DENV-4). It is given as an injection under the skin, in two doses three months apart . A booster dose is not currently part of the approved schedule. Malaysia’s Drug Control Authority gave it conditional registration in February 2024 . That means the company must keep submitting safety and effectiveness data. A renewal of the conditional registration has been reported from February 2026. The vaccine is not in the National Immunisation Programme . In August 2026, the Health Minister said the Ministry was still studying whether to include it, including a cost-benefit analysis. For now, it is only offered privately. In Malaysia, it is registered for people aged 4 and above , whether or not they have had dengue before. There is little data for people over 60. The World Health Organization recommends it mainly for children aged 6 to 16 in areas with high dengue transmission, and says people up to 60 with conditions such as diabetes or high blood pressure may also be offered it. You should not have it if you: are pregnant or breastfeeding (and you should avoid becoming pregnant for at least a month afterwards) have a weakened immune system, for example from chemotherapy, high-dose steroids or HIV with low immunity had a severe allergic reaction to a previous dose or to any ingredient If you have a high fever on the day, the vaccination should be delayed. The main trial followed about 20,000 children aged 4 to 16 in Asia and Latin America. Four and a half years after the second dose, the vaccine had reduced: Group Fewer dengue cases Fewer hospital admissions Everyone 61% 84% Had dengue before 64% 86% Never had dengue 54% 79% Protection was highest in the first year and a half, and lowest in children aged 4 to 5. Protection was not the same against every dengue type. In people who had never had dengue , the trial found good protection against DENV-2 and some against DENV-1, but no protection against DENV-3 , and too few DENV-4 cases to show any benefit. The few cases of severe dengue in vaccinated people who had never had dengue were all DENV-3. The difference was not statistically significant, but WHO says a higher risk “cannot be conclusively ruled out”. In people who had dengue before, the vaccine did protect against DENV-3, cutting hospital admissions by about three-quarters. Why this matters in 2026 DENV-3 is now the main dengue type in Malaysia. If you have never had dengue, or don’t know, talk this through with your doctor before deciding. They can explain the likely benefit for you and your family. Most side effects are mild to moderate, start within two days and last one to three days. They are less common after the second dose. In trials: Pain at the injection site: 50% Headache: 35% Muscle aches: 31% Redness at the injection site: 27% Feeling unwell or tired: 20–24% Fever: 11% Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) are rare, so you will be asked to wait at the clinic for a short time afterwards. Because it is a live vaccine, some people briefly have the vaccine virus in their blood, and a dengue test taken soon after vaccination may be positive. Tell the doctor you were recently vaccinated if you need a dengue test. Because the vaccine is only available privately, each clinic sets its own price. News reports from 2024 to 2026 put the cost of both doses at roughly RM400 to RM500 in total. Ask for the full price, including the consultation, before your first dose. Vaccination costs can be claimed under the medical expenses tax relief for vaccinations. Keep your receipt. No dengue vaccine gives complete protection. Keep doing the basics: Clear standing water around your home every week, including plant saucers, roof gutters and containers. Use mosquito repellent and cover up during the early morning and late afternoon. Know the early symptoms and warning signs of dengue . Severe stomach pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding gums or drowsiness need urgent care. Is the dengue vaccine approved in Malaysia? Yes, conditionally. Qdenga received conditional registration from Malaysia’s Drug Control Authority in February 2024 for people aged 4 and above, and a renewal has been reported from February 2026. Is the dengue vaccine free in Malaysia? No. It is not part of the National Immunisation Programme, so it is only available at private clinics and hospitals. The Health Ministry said in 2026 that it is still studying whether to include it. How much is the dengue vaccine in Malaysia? News reports from 2024 to 2026 put the cost of both doses at roughly RM400 to RM500 in total at private clinics. Prices vary, so ask before booking. Should I get the dengue vaccine if I have never had dengue? Talk to your doctor first. In people who had never had dengue, the vaccine did not protect against DENV-3 in trials, and DENV-3 is the main dengue type in Malaysia in 2026. Can I get dengue after the vaccine? Yes. The vaccine lowers the risk of dengue and especially of hospital admission, but it does not give complete protection. Keep preventing mosquito bites and watch for warning signs.

title: HPV vaccine in Malaysia 2026: the school programme, catch-up options and adults
desc: From 2026, Year 6 girls get a single free HPV dose at school. What changed, how to catch up if you missed it, options for boys and adults, and why screening still matters.
headings: Why the HPV vaccine matters · The school programme: what changed in 2026 · If your daughter missed it · HPV vaccine for boys and adults · How much does it cost? · Vaccinated? You still need screening · Side effects and safety
keywords: Women's health HPV vaccine in Malaysia Human papillomavirus infection Jangkitan HPV mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: From 2026, girls get the HPV vaccine free in Year 6 (age 12) at school, instead of Form 1. The programme now gives a single dose. Budget 2027 upgrades the school vaccine from the bivalent (2-type) vaccine to the nonavalent (9-type) vaccine. Girls who missed the school programme can book at government clinics through MySejahtera. Boys and adult women are not covered by the national programme, but can be vaccinated privately or through subsidised NGO programmes. Vaccinated women still need cervical screening: an HPV test every 5 years from age 30. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a very common virus spread through sexual contact. Most infections clear on their own, but long-lasting infection with high-risk types can cause cervical cancer, as well as some cancers of the throat, anus and genitals. Cervical cancer is one of the most common cancers in Malaysian women. WHO’s cancer agency estimates 1,968 new cases and 964 deaths a year, making it the third most common cancer in women. The National Cancer Registry, which counts recorded cases, ranks it sixth and found that 47% of cases were diagnosed at stage 3 or 4 , when treatment is harder. Malaysia aims for 90% of girls to be vaccinated by age 15 by 2030, as part of its plan to eliminate cervical cancer. The vaccine works best when given before any exposure to HPV, which is why it is offered at age 12. Earlier: from 2026, the free vaccine is given to girls in Year 6 (age 12) instead of Form 1 (age 13). The Ministry of Health says this gives protection earlier, in line with WHO advice, and means fewer girls are missed when they change school. One dose: Malaysia moved from three doses (2010) to two (2015) to a single dose . WHO’s vaccine experts confirmed in October 2026 that one dose is the most efficient approach for girls aged 9 to 14. A broader vaccine from 2027: schools currently use a bivalent vaccine, which protects against HPV types 16 and 18, the cause of most cervical cancers. Budget 2027 upgrades this to a nonavalent (9-type) vaccine for about 230,000 Year 6 girls. Parents or guardians must give written consent . Schools send home the consent form and an information leaflet about a week before vaccination day. Between 2020 and 2024, a global vaccine shortage meant many Malaysian girls missed their school dose. First-dose coverage fell from over 95% to about 35% in 2024. The Ministry ran a catch-up programme for these cohorts in schools in 2024 and early 2025. Girls who missed the school programme, including those in private schools or home-schooled, can book at a government health clinic through MySejahtera . The National Cancer Society Malaysia (NCSM) also runs a subsidised programme in 2026 for boys and girls aged 9 to 14 , at RM290 per dose at partner clinics. The national programme covers girls only. Boys and adults can be vaccinated at private clinics and hospitals. HPV vaccination helps protect men against genital warts and some cancers, and reduces spread of the virus. How many doses you need depends on your age and the vaccine used. Under the product label of the nonavalent vaccine, people aged 9 to 14 usually need two doses, and people aged 15 and over usually need three doses over six months. People with weakened immune systems may need more doses. Your doctor will advise on the right schedule. WHO advises that catch-up vaccination should prioritise young women up to age 25, then up to 30, followed by boys aged 9 to 14. Vaccination works best before any exposure to HPV, so the benefit for older adults is usually smaller. The school programme is free. At private clinics, news reports in 2026 said the HPV vaccine typically costs around RM500 , depending on the vaccine and clinic, compared with RM290 per dose through NCSM’s subsidised programme for ages 9 to 14. Ask for the total cost of the full course before you start. Vaccination costs for yourself, your spouse and your children can be claimed under the medical expenses tax relief for vaccinations. The vaccine does not protect against every high-risk HPV type, and it does not clear an existing infection. Women should still be screened: Aged 30 to 49: an HPV test, repeated every 5 years if negative. You can often take the sample yourself. Aged 21 to 29 and 50 to 65: a Pap smear. Free options include government health clinics, the Ministry of Health’s ROSE programme at government hospitals, and free HPV tests for eligible women aged 30 to 65 at LPPKN’s Klinik Nur Sejahtera. About 65% of women in the ROSE programme had not been screened in the previous three years. See a doctor if you notice Bleeding between periods, after sex or after menopause Unusual vaginal discharge Pelvic pain or pain during sex The HPV vaccine has been used worldwide for more than 15 years and has a strong safety record. Common side effects are redness, swelling or pain at the injection site. Less common are mild fever, headache or joint pain. Some young people faint after any injection, so you will be asked to sit for about 15 minutes afterwards. Severe allergic reactions are very rare. The vaccine is not recommended during pregnancy as a precaution. If you become pregnant partway through a course, the remaining doses are given after delivery. Is the HPV vaccine free in Malaysia? Yes, for girls through the school programme, which from 2026 vaccinates girls in Year 6. Girls who missed it can book at a government clinic through MySejahtera. Boys and adults pay at private clinics, or can use subsidised NGO programmes. How many doses of HPV vaccine do Malaysian schoolgirls get? One. The national programme moved to a single-dose schedule, which WHO says is effective for girls aged 9 to 14. Can adults get the HPV vaccine in Malaysia? Yes, at private clinics and hospitals. Adults aged 15 and over usually need three doses. Ask your doctor whether vaccination is likely to benefit you. Can boys get the HPV vaccine in Malaysia? Yes, privately. The national programme covers girls only, but in 2026 the National Cancer Society Malaysia offered subsidised vaccination for boys and girls aged 9 to 14. Do I still need a Pap smear or HPV test if I had the vaccine? Yes. The vaccine does not cover every cancer-causing HPV type. Women aged 30 to 49 should have an HPV test every 5 years, and Pap smears are used at ages 21 to 29 and 50 to 65.

title: Pico laser for melasma in Malaysia: what it can do, the risks, and the 2026 rules
desc: Pico laser is heavily advertised for melasma and pigmentation. What the evidence shows, why melasma keeps coming back, the risks for Asian skin, and Malaysia’s new laser rules.
headings: What is melasma? · Why melasma keeps coming back · Treatments to try first · What pico laser is, and what it can do · Risks for Asian and darker skin · Malaysia’s 2026 rules on aesthetic lasers · How to check a clinic before booking · A warning about whitening creams
keywords: Aesthetics & skin Pico laser for melasma Melasma mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Melasma is a long-term skin condition. Treatments can fade it, but none cure it, and it often comes back. Daily sunscreen, ideally a tinted one with iron oxides, and prescription creams from a doctor are the first-line treatment. Lasers, including pico lasers, are usually kept for melasma that hasn’t improved with creams. They can make pigmentation worse in darker skin. Since 1 June 2026, many aesthetic lasers are “designated medical devices” in Malaysia. Operating one without a permit is an offence. Avoid whitening creams sold online. NPRA has cancelled several in 2026 for containing mercury, hydroquinone or tretinoin. Melasma is a common condition that causes flat, brown or grey-brown patches, usually on both cheeks, the forehead, upper lip, nose or chin. It is not itchy, infectious or cancerous. It is most common in women aged 20 to 40 and in people with light-brown to brown skin, including many Malaysians. Triggers include sunlight (both UV and visible light), hormones such as pregnancy, the contraceptive pill and hormone therapy, and a family tendency . Up to half of pregnant women may develop some melasma. It is easily confused with other pigmentation, which is treated differently: Sunspots (solar lentigines): separate, well-defined brown spots on sun-damaged skin. Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation : dark marks left after acne, eczema or injury. Hori’s naevus : deeper, blue-grey patches, often on the cheeks. Because the right treatment depends on the type, a doctor should diagnose your pigmentation before any laser. There is no cure for melasma. Even after a good result, sun exposure or hormonal changes can bring it back, and it often returns after treatment stops. Pregnancy-related melasma may fade after delivery but can return in a later pregnancy. That is why dermatologists treat melasma as a long-term condition that needs ongoing sun protection and, often, maintenance treatment. Be cautious of any clinic that promises permanent removal. Sun protection every day: a broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher. A tinted sunscreen containing iron oxides also blocks visible light. In one trial it gave better results than a UV-only sunscreen. Reapply outdoors and wear a hat. Prescription creams: creams that combine a lightening agent with a retinoid and a mild steroid are considered the most effective first treatment, improving 60–80% of cases. They must be prescribed and supervised by a doctor, used for limited periods, and avoided in pregnancy. Other options your doctor may suggest include azelaic acid, and tablets or creams containing tranexamic acid. Tranexamic acid tablets are a medicine that needs a doctor’s assessment, as they are not suitable for everyone. A doctor should confirm the type of pigmentation before recommending treatment. Picosecond (“pico”) lasers fire extremely short pulses of light, measured in trillionths of a second. The pulses shatter pigment mainly through a pressure effect rather than heat, using less energy than older nanosecond (Q-switched) lasers. The evidence differs by use: Use What studies show Tattoo removal Strongest evidence Melasma Can help, especially with the 1064 nm wavelength. Results are often similar to, not better than, prescription creams, and melasma usually returns without maintenance Acne scars Moderate improvement over about six sessions with a fractional lens Sunspots and freckles Often respond well, but are a different condition from melasma For melasma, a 2023 analysis of trials found the 1064 nm pico laser effective without significant side effects, while the 755 nm laser was no better than creams and more likely to cause darkening. A 2026 review concluded that no single device is a definitive answer, and that maintenance is crucial. Brown skin is more prone to pigment changes after any laser. Possible effects include: Darkening (post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation), usually temporary but sometimes lasting months. Rebound melasma , where melasma comes back darker. Patchy white spots (mottled hypopigmentation), reported in about 10% of East Asian patients after repeated low-energy “laser toning”, and linked to too much total energy. Redness, swelling, blistering and, rarely, scarring or burns, which are more common when an untrained person operates the laser. Avoid sun exposure before and after treatment, and tell the doctor if you are pregnant, take medicines that make the skin sensitive to light, or get cold sores. Since 1 June 2026 , the Medical Device (Designated Medical Device) Order 2026 lists many aesthetic lasers as designated medical devices . These include Nd:YAG (532 and 1064 nm), alexandrite, ruby, diode, fractional CO2 and other lasers when used to reduce pigmentation such as melasma and freckles, or for other aesthetic purposes. HIFU devices are also covered. Under the Medical Device Act 2012, no one may operate a designated medical device without a permit . The penalty is a fine of up to RM100,000, up to a year in prison, or both. The Medical Device Authority says operators must have qualifications and skills recognised by the government. The Ministry of Health’s guidelines also class lasers for pigmentation as an aesthetic medical procedure, to be done by a registered doctor with the right training and credentials, in a registered clinic. A medical-grade laser in a salon or spa is a red flag. Doctor: look them up on the Malaysian Medical Council’s MeRITS register and ask whether they hold a Letter of Credentialing and Privileging (LCP) for aesthetic procedures. Clinic: it should be registered with the Ministry of Health, not a salon or home business. Device: ask which laser will be used and check it on the MDA medical device register . Plan: ask for a diagnosis, the expected number of sessions, the risks for your skin type, what happens if pigmentation gets worse, and a written quote. Many people with melasma try lightening creams bought online. Some contain hidden ingredients. In 2025 and 2026, the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) cancelled the notification of 20 cosmetic products for containing mercury , hydroquinone or tretinoin . Half of them contained mercury. Mercury is banned in cosmetics. It can damage the kidneys and nerves, and harm the developing brain of an unborn baby or young child. Hydroquinone and tretinoin are medicines in Malaysia, not cosmetic ingredients. They should only be used with a health professional’s advice. Check a product on NPRA’s list of cancelled cosmetics before using it, and stop using any cream that is not properly labelled. See a doctor if a patch is changing in size, shape or colour bleeds, itches or doesn’t heal appears on only one side, or looks different from your other marks Can pico laser remove melasma permanently? No. Pico laser can lighten melasma, but no treatment cures it, and melasma often returns, especially with sun exposure or hormonal changes. Ongoing sun protection and maintenance are usually needed. Is pico laser safe for Malaysian skin? It can be, in trained hands with suitable settings. Brown skin has a higher risk of darkening, rebound melasma and white spots after lasers, so a doctor should assess your skin and start cautiously. How many pico laser sessions are needed for melasma? Studies used anywhere from three to about ten sessions, usually several weeks apart, followed by maintenance. Your doctor should give you a plan based on your skin. Who is allowed to do laser treatment in Malaysia? Since 1 June 2026, many aesthetic lasers are designated medical devices, and operating one requires a permit from the Medical Device Authority. MOH guidelines also class laser pigmentation treatment as a medical procedure for trained, registered doctors in registered clinics. What is the best treatment for melasma? Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen, ideally tinted with iron oxides, plus prescription creams supervised by a doctor, is the usual first-line treatment. Lasers are generally kept for melasma that doesn’t respond.

title: Skin boosters in Malaysia: Profhilo, Rejuran, Juvelook and exosomes explained
desc: What Profhilo, Rejuran, Juvelook and other skin boosters actually do, how many sessions they take, the risks, and how to check a clinic and product are legal.
headings: What are skin boosters? · How many sessions, and how long do results last? · Is it legal? What Malaysian rules say · How to check the doctor, clinic and product (the 3Ps) · Side effects and risks · Questions to ask at your consultation · How much do skin boosters cost?
keywords: Aesthetics & skin Skin boosters in Malaysia payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: “Skin booster” covers several different injectables: hyaluronic acid (such as Profhilo), polynucleotides (such as Rejuran) and collagen stimulators (such as Juvelook and Sculptra). These products are regulated as medical devices. Check that a product is on the Medical Device Authority (MDA) register. Only a registered doctor with a Letter of Credentialing and Privileging (LCP) may inject them, at an MOH-registered clinic. No exosome product appears on the MDA register, and cosmetics in Malaysia are for use on the skin only, not injection. Never have injections at homes, hotels or beauty salons. MOH calls this “checking the 3Ps”: procedure, practitioner and premises. “Skin booster” is a marketing term rather than a medical one. It usually means small amounts of an injectable placed just under the skin to improve hydration, texture, fine lines or firmness, rather than to add volume the way a lip or cheek filler does. The main types work quite differently: Type Examples How it works Hyaluronic acid (HA) Profhilo, Restylane Skinboosters, NCTF 135 HA Hyaluronic acid holds water in the skin, improving hydration and smoothness Polynucleotides (PN) Rejuran DNA fragments said to support skin repair; mostly studied in Korea Collagen stimulators Juvelook (PDLLA), Sculptra (PLLA) Microparticles trigger the skin to build collagen gradually over months Exosomes Various “exosome” serums Not registered as an injectable; see below Injectable treatments should only take place in an MOH-registered clinic. Hyaluronic acid boosters: in one study of Profhilo, women had two treatments four weeks apart, and improvement was still measurable at 16 weeks. Polynucleotides: a 2024 review found most studies used three to four sessions about two weeks apart. The authors noted the evidence is still limited and of low-to-moderate quality. Collagen stimulators: results build slowly. In the US trial for Sculptra, people had up to four sessions, and many still showed improvement two years later. Results vary between people, and most treatments need top-up sessions to maintain them. Be cautious of any promise of a fixed result or a fixed number of months. Skin booster injectables are regulated in Malaysia as medical devices . Products sold here must be registered with the Medical Device Authority (MDA). As of October 2026, the MDA register lists products including Profhilo, Rejuran, Sculptra, Restylane Skinboosters and NCTF 135 HA. You can search it yourself on the MDA medical device register . The Ministry of Health lists filler injections as a minimally invasive aesthetic procedure. They may only be done by a registered doctor holding a Letter of Credentialing and Privileging (LCP) , in premises registered under the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998. A note on exosomes: searching the MDA register for “exosome” returns no products. In Malaysia, cosmetics are legally for use on the outside of the body, so a cosmetic exosome serum is not approved for injection. Doctors have reported cases of skin damage and scarring after exosome products meant for the skin were injected. The Ministry of Health urges the public to “check the 3Ps” before any aesthetic procedure: Practitioner: look the doctor up on the Malaysian Medical Council’s MeRITS register , and check MOH’s national registry of doctors with an LCP . Premises: the clinic should be registered with MOH. MOH publishes its list of registered private clinics, including those offering aesthetic services. Procedure and product: ask for the product’s name and check it on the MDA register. Make sure the procedure is one MOH allows. Breast and buttock fillers, for example, are illegal in Malaysia. Avoid injections at homes, hotels or salons In September 2026, raids in Shah Alam, Pandan Perdana and Kepong found unlicensed “therapists” offering aesthetic treatments in rented homes, promoted on TikTok and Instagram. Cheaper prices from unlicensed operators often mean unregistered products and no one to treat complications. Common, usually short-lived effects include bruising, redness, swelling, tenderness and small bumps at the injection points, which typically settle within days to a week. Less common but important risks: Lumps and nodules , particularly with collagen stimulators. In the Sculptra trial, 17% of patients developed nodules or bumps, sometimes appearing months later. Unlike hyaluronic acid, these cannot be dissolved with an enzyme. Injection into a blood vessel . This is rare but serious, and can cause skin damage, vision loss or stroke. It is the main reason injections should only be done by trained doctors who can recognise and treat it immediately. Infection and allergic reactions. Seek urgent medical care for severe or increasing pain, skin that turns pale, blue or dusky, or any change in your vision after an injection. Which product will you use, and is it registered with the MDA? Do you hold an LCP for this procedure? What results can I realistically expect, and how many sessions? What are the risks for me, and what happens if there is a complication? What is the total cost, including follow-up sessions? A careful doctor will review your medical history, medicines and allergies, explain alternatives, and give you time to decide. Be wary of pressure to book on the spot. Prices depend on the product, the amount used and the number of sessions. In October 2026, clinic adverts in Malaysia commonly listed skin booster treatments from around RM500 to over RM3,000 per session . Ask for a written quote that includes all planned sessions. A much lower price can be a warning sign of unregistered products or an unlicensed provider. Are skin boosters safe? When a registered product is injected by a trained, LCP-holding doctor in a registered clinic, side effects are usually mild and short-lived, such as bruising and swelling. Serious complications are rare but possible, which is why the doctor and clinic matter. Is exosome injection approved in Malaysia? No exosome product appears on the Medical Device Authority register, and cosmetics in Malaysia are legally for use on the skin, not injection. Ask your doctor exactly what product they plan to use and check its registration. How long do skin boosters last? It depends on the type. Hyaluronic acid boosters are usually repeated every few months, while collagen stimulators work gradually and can last longer. Most people need top-up sessions. Can a beautician do skin booster injections in Malaysia? No. Filler injections are a medical procedure in Malaysia. They may only be done by a registered doctor with a Letter of Credentialing and Privileging (LCP), in an MOH-registered clinic. How much is a skin booster in Malaysia? In October 2026, clinic adverts commonly listed skin boosters from around RM500 to over RM3,000 per session, depending on the product and number of sessions. Ask for a written quote.

title: Weight-loss injections in Malaysia: what Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro can and can’t do
desc: Which injections are actually registered for weight loss in Malaysia, who they’re meant for, the side effects, and why “slimming pens” sold online are risky.
headings: What these injections are · Which ones are registered in Malaysia? · Who are they for? · How much weight do people lose? · Side effects and safety · Why “slimming pens” sold online are risky · What to expect when you see a doctor

body: These medicines (GLP-1 medicines such as semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide) are prescription-only in Malaysia. Only a registered doctor can prescribe them. Wegovy, Saxenda and Mounjaro are registered for weight management. Ozempic is registered for type 2 diabetes, not weight loss. They are meant for adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related condition, alongside diet and exercise. Stomach side effects are common, and most people regain weight after stopping. Never buy “slimming pens” online or from salons. MOH has raided sellers and removed hundreds of listings in 2026. The injections people search for, such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro, belong to a group of medicines that copy gut hormones called GLP-1 (and, for tirzepatide, also GIP). They make you feel full sooner, slow down how quickly the stomach empties, and help control blood sugar. Most are injected once a week with a pre-filled pen. In Malaysia they are Group B poisons under the Poisons Act 1952 . That means they can only be supplied by a registered doctor, or by a pharmacist with a doctor’s prescription. Selling them any other way is an offence. Every medicine sold legally in Malaysia carries a registration number starting with MAL , listed by the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA). More than half of Malaysian adults (54.4%) are overweight or obese, according to the National Health and Morbidity Survey 2023. But these medicines are not meant for losing a few kilos before a holiday. The registered labels allow them for adults with: a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or more , or a BMI of 27 or more with at least one weight-related condition, such as prediabetes or type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, sleep apnoea or heart disease. In the tirzepatide trial, average weight loss at the highest dose was about 21% over 72 weeks. Results vary a lot between people, and they depend on staying on treatment and keeping up healthy habits. The weight tends to come back after stopping. In one study, people regained about two-thirds of the weight they had lost within a year of stopping semaglutide. They are not for use in pregnancy , and the product information advises stopping them before a planned pregnancy. People with a personal or family history of a rare thyroid cancer (medullary thyroid carcinoma) should not use semaglutide or tirzepatide. Between January and July 2026, its Pharmacy Enforcement Division carried out 30 raids on weight-loss products, 17 of them involving online sales, and seized goods worth RM477,142. It also took down 209 e-commerce listings. Pens bought outside a clinic or pharmacy may be fake, unregistered, wrongly stored or the wrong dose. Check the hologram security label (FarmaTag) with the FarmaChecker feature in the MyUBAT app. Avoid sellers on social media, e-commerce sites and in beauty salons. A doctor will usually ask about your weight history, eating habits, activity, sleep and other medicines. They will measure your weight, waist and blood pressure, and may arrange blood tests for blood sugar, cholesterol, and liver and kidney function. If a medicine is suitable, it is started at a low dose and increased slowly, with follow-up visits to check side effects and progress. A good weight-management plan also covers food, movement and sleep, and agrees what success looks like for you. For some people with a very high BMI, the doctor may discuss bariatric surgery. Is Ozempic approved for weight loss in Malaysia? No. In Malaysia, Ozempic is registered for type 2 diabetes. Wegovy, which contains a higher dose of the same medicine (semaglutide), is the version registered for weight management. Is Mounjaro available for weight loss in Malaysia? Mounjaro (tirzepatide) is registered in Malaysia, and its current product information includes weight management as well as type 2 diabetes. These medicines are Group B poisons that need a prescription, and the Ministry of Health has raided sellers and removed online listings in 2026. Pens sold online may be fake or unregistered. Will I regain weight if I stop the injections? Many people do. Studies show a large part of the weight lost often returns within a year of stopping, which is why doctors pair medicines with long-term lifestyle changes.

title: How to check your blood pressure at home: a five-minute routine
desc: How to sit, when to measure, and what numbers to bring to your doctor, following Malaysia’s clinical guidelines.
headings: Why measure at home? · Choosing a monitor · The five-minute routine · What the numbers mean · Bringing readings to your doctor
keywords: Heart & diabetes Checking blood pressure at home Hypertension Darah tinggi darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Use a validated, automatic upper-arm monitor with the right cuff size. Sit quietly with your back and arm supported for a few minutes before measuring. Take two readings, one minute apart, every morning and evening for up to seven days. Malaysian guidelines treat an average home reading above 135/85 mmHg as elevated. Blood pressure changes through the day, and some people read higher at the clinic simply because they are anxious (“white-coat” hypertension). Others read normal at the clinic but high at home. Malaysia’s Clinical Practice Guidelines on hypertension encourage home monitoring because it helps with diagnosis, empowers patients and can improve how well treatment works. Upper-arm, automatic. Wrist and finger monitors are less reliable. Validated for accuracy. Ask your pharmacist for a clinically validated model. The right cuff size. A cuff that is too small gives falsely high readings. Measure around your upper arm and check the range printed on the cuff. Memory function is handy, so you do not have to write every reading down. Prepare. No smoking, eating, caffeine or exercise for 30 minutes beforehand. Empty your bladder. Sit well. Back supported, feet flat, legs uncrossed, arm resting on a table so the cuff is at heart level. Rest quietly for a few minutes. No talking or scrolling. Measure twice , at least one minute apart, on bare skin. Record both readings straight away, with the date and time. Measure at about the same time in the morning (before medicines, if you take them) and in the evening (before dinner), for at least three days and ideally seven. Keep a simple logbook, or use a monitor that stores readings. Ignore the readings from the first day, then average the rest. According to Malaysia’s Clinical Practice Guidelines (Management of Hypertension, 5th edition), an average home reading above 135/85 mmHg should be considered elevated. Bring your logbook to your doctor, who will interpret it together with your clinic readings. Get help quickly See a doctor the same day if readings are repeatedly 180/110 mmHg or higher. Call 999 if a high reading comes with chest pain, breathlessness, weakness on one side, slurred speech or a sudden severe headache. Take your logbook or monitor to your next appointment. If you are on treatment, home readings help your doctor adjust your medicines safely. If you have never been diagnosed but your average is high, book a check-up. High blood pressure is very treatable, and lifestyle changes alone often help in the early stages. What is a normal home blood pressure reading? Malaysia’s hypertension guidelines treat an average home reading above 135/85 mmHg as elevated. Your doctor will advise on your personal target. Are wrist blood pressure monitors accurate? Upper-arm monitors are generally more reliable. If you use a wrist monitor, keep your wrist at heart level and check it against a clinic reading. Should I measure before or after taking my medicine? Measure in the morning before taking your blood pressure medicine, and in the evening before dinner.

body: Call 999 (or 112 from a mobile) for life-threatening emergencies. Go to an emergency department for urgent problems that cannot wait, such as dengue warning signs. For most fevers, coughs, minor injuries and ongoing conditions, a GP clinic is faster and better suited. Chest pain or pressure, especially spreading to the arm, jaw or back Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness, slurred speech. Note the time symptoms started. Severe difficulty breathing, or blue lips Unconsciousness, a seizure, or sudden confusion Heavy bleeding that will not stop A severe allergic reaction with swelling of the face or throat Serious injury, such as after a road accident or a fall from height From a mobile phone you can also dial 112 . Dengue warning signs: severe stomach pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, or drowsiness (see our dengue guide ) A fever of 38°C or higher in a baby under three months old Severe abdominal pain Suspected broken bones, deep cuts or burns Dehydration in a child who is not passing urine Heavy bleeding or severe pain in pregnancy Malaysian emergency departments use a triage colour system (red, yellow, green). The most urgent patients are seen first, so less urgent cases may wait longer. That is one reason a GP is often quicker for non-urgent problems. Most fevers, coughs, colds and sore throats A fever lasting more than two days (for a dengue blood test) Minor cuts, sprains and wound dressing Rashes, ear pain, urinary symptoms Diabetes, blood pressure and cholesterol follow-up Health screening, vaccinations, and medical certificates Mental health concerns, when there is no immediate danger A GP can treat most everyday illnesses and refer you to a hospital if needed. Government health clinics ( klinik kesihatan ) offer low-cost care, especially for long-term conditions, antenatal care and child vaccinations, but they usually keep office hours. Private GP clinics often open into the evening and on weekends, which helps when illness strikes after work. Many accept company panels or insurance, so bring your panel card. Dial 999 from any phone. From a mobile phone you can also dial 112. Should I go to a clinic or the emergency department for a high fever? For most adults and older children, a GP clinic is the right first stop. Go to the emergency department for a baby under three months with a fever of 38°C or more, or for dengue warning signs such as severe stomach pain, bleeding or persistent vomiting.
